A world model from pixels

Module 31 · Acting and planning ← All explorables

A small JEPA world model learned two rooms from 64 × 64 frames: an encoder turns a frame into 32 numbers, a predictor guesses the next 32 numbers from the current ones and five moves. Two losses only: the prediction error, and SIGReg, which keeps the 32 numbers spread like a Gaussian. A planner then searches for moves whose imagined end lands closest to the goal's 32 numbers. This page holds the module's trained predictor and plans in your browser.

1 · Drop the agent and the goal, watch CEM search

Click to place the agent or the goal. The shading is the planner's cost: the squared distance between the 32 numbers of a frame with the agent there and those of the goal frame (dark = near; only the nearest 30% of spots are shaded). CEM, the cross-entropy method, draws plans from a Gaussian, keeps the cheapest, refits the Gaussian to them and repeats; random shooting draws all its plans at once and keeps the cheapest. Plan once runs one search, a few seconds; the slider then shows its rounds: the 12 best imagined paths of each round, read back into positions by a linear probe. Run takes the first five moves of each plan in the real world and plans again, up to 30 times.

Search rounds of the last plan

The line: mean distance of the 12 best imagined end points from their centre, per round. CEM narrows its search each round; random shooting has one round.

The page runs the module's predictor in 16-bit floats with its own random numbers. In place of the encoder it reads a 48 × 48 table of the encoder's outputs, made by the module, between the table's points by straight-line mixing. A run here can differ from the module's runs.

2 · The module's recorded runs

Ten test tasks of each kind, as the module ran them with 300 candidates a round. Solid: the real path. Dotted: the first plans, as the probe reads them. For CEM the slider shows the first plan's rounds.

3 · What each training recipe learned

Three seeds each. Probe R²: how much of the agent's position a linear read-out recovers from the 32 (or 8, or 192) numbers (1 = all). Effective rank: how many directions the numbers really use. Spearman: does latent distance rank pairs of frames the way the walk between them does?

4 · Module 25's grid, with the extra terms

Module 25's grid JEPA dropped the agent from its latent. Switch a term on and see what the probe reads and how often the same random-shooting planner reaches the goal (300 arenas, three seeds). The boards replay seed 0 on four test arenas. A follow-up, written after the results, gives the planner the goal's cell from outside and asks the latent only for the agent.
